# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

## What this repo is

An experiment comparing how well AI builds a three.js tropical beach scene. One shared base scene (water, sky, sand, light) with 8 prop slots, where only the prop source varies:

- **A**: procedural props written by codex.
- **B**: Tripo AI GLBs, decimated in Blender.
  - Exception: since 2026-10-20 the lifeguard tower is a Tripo image-to-model build (`tools/tripo_image_tower.py`) from a Codex reference image (`assets/raw/lifeguard_ladder/`) that adds a ladder and a railing opening. The text-prompt tower had no ladder. Blind scores and REPORT figures predate this swap.
- **C**: free library models (Poly Haven, Sketchfab, Poly Pizza).

On top of that there are an explore mode, a synced split-view compare page, a game mode, three characters (A/B/C), blind scoring, and comparison videos and slides.

Read these first:

- `PLAYBOOK.md`: the reusable process, commands and pitfalls.
- `NOTES.md`: per-feature implementation notes, written by codex.
- `REPORT.md` and `心得.md`: results.

User-facing docs are in Traditional Chinese (Taiwan); keep that.

Sibling worktrees `../beach3d-codex2` (port 5193) and `../beach3d-opus` (port 5192) hold the same pipeline re-run by other models (branches `codex2-run`, `opus-run`). They share only `assets/props.json` and the recorder hooks below.

## Commands

```sh
npx vite --port 5191 --strictPort      # dev server (npm run dev); many scripts assume 5191
npm run build                          # 6 entries: index, scene, compare, props, game, tidepool → dist/ (copies assets/, report/)
node scripts/shoot.mjs <A|B|C>         # fixed-camera stills → shots/<g>/{wide,beach,closeup}.png (SwiftShader)
node scripts/shoot-props.mjs <g> [slot]   # solo prop renders → shots/<g>/props/
node scripts/verify-game.mjs           # full game regression (quests, tide pool, open sea, boat, A/B/C, mobile, missing GLBs)
node scripts/verify-tidepool.mjs       # tide-pool page A/B/C: lift stones, observe 6, mobile → shots/tidepool/
node scripts/verify-explore.mjs        # explore-mode regression
node scripts/probe-clip.mjs [actions] [groups]   # clipping audit: rest,tower,boat,shell,ball × A/B/C (SNAP=1 stills → shots/clip/, DETAIL=1 surfaces)
```

Media pipeline:

- `node scripts/record-path.mjs <g> [fps] [path.json] [outdir]`: frame-by-frame GPU render along a camera path. Uses `SCENE_URL` and `SETTLE_MS` to point at other ports.
- `scripts/record-game.mjs` and `scripts/record-walk.mjs <g>`: game and character recordings.
- `node scripts/record-tidepool.mjs <g> [fps]` → `video/frames/tidepool_<g>/`, then `python3 tools/make_tidepool.py` → `video/tidepool_abc.mp4` (A/B/C side by side, same action timeline).
- `node scripts/record-game-tidepool.mjs [g]` → `video/game_tidepool.mp4` (walk to the pool in the game, observe all 6, return).
- `node scripts/record-game-opensea.mjs <g>` → `video/frames/opensea_<g>/`, `video/game_opensea_<g>.mp4` and `video/opensea_<g>.json` (observation times). Same boat and camera path for every group: row to 10 m from the buoy, turn once in place, press E when a prompt shows (at least 2.5 s apart). `DRY=1` only simulates. Then `python3 tools/make_opensea.py` → `video/opensea_abc.mp4`. The slides use re-encoded copies (crf 27) in `slides/assets/`.
- Compositing: `python3 tools/make_video.py`, `tools/make_zoom.py`, `tools/compare_models.py`.

Assets and stats:

- `.venv/bin/python tools/tripo_gen.py --dry-run|<slots>|--recover <task> <slot>`: Tripo generation. Spends credits, so ask the user first.
- `tools/decimate_all.sh`: Blender headless decimation to 30k tris.
- `tools/build_stats.py` → `report/stats.json`; `tools/compare.py` → `compare/*.png`.

Blind scoring:

- `tools/blind_score.py`; set `BLIND_CONFIG` to compare other dirs.
- `tools/blind_props.py`; `tools/judge_opus.py` runs Opus as a second judge.

Slides:

- `tools/build_live.sh` packages the three versions into `slides/live/`.
- `cd slides && python3 start.py` serves the slides and live demos (`live/`) on port 8730.

Delegation to other models:

- `tools/codex_run.sh <group> <step> <BRIEF.md>`: runs codex exec on a brief, timed via `tools/timed.sh` into `timing.csv`.
- Opus runs use `tools/claude_run.sh` in the opus worktree.

There is no lint or unit-test setup. Verification means running the Playwright scripts and looking at the screenshots.

## Architecture

- **One scene module, many pages.** `src/main.js` builds the renderer, sky, sand, water (`src/water.js`), coast details and the prop root for every page. It switches behaviour by URL and pathname:
  - `?cam=` gives a fixed view.
  - `?explore=1` lazy-loads `src/explore.js`.
  - `compare.html` adds `src/compare.js`, which uses one renderer with scissor viewports and toggles props per pane.
  - `game.html` adds `src/game/*`.
  - `props.html` runs `src/props-solo.js`, a separate solo viewer.
  - `tidepool.html` runs `src/tidepool/`, its own small scene that does not import `src/main.js`.
  - `index.html` is the hub (`src/hub.js`, reads `report/stats.json`).
- **Props.** `assets/props.json` is the single source of slots: `pos`, `height`, optional `maxLen`, `prompt`, and `paths.B/C` GLB paths. `src/props.js` `loadProps(group)` places either A's procedural builders (`src/props-a.js`) or GLBs.
  - `?swapB=<slot>:<glb path>` swaps one B prop for a trial, without touching `props.json` (same fit rule).
  - The fit rule is shared by all groups: `scale = min(height/size.y, maxLen/max(size.x,size.z))`. Don't change it per group, or the comparison stops being fair.
  - Grounding (since 2026-10-21, all groups): after the box bottom is put on the sand under the slot, `settle()` shifts the prop so the median gap of its lowest 6 cm of vertices to the sand is zero (on the slope the seaward side used to float up to ~15 cm). `node scripts/probe-ground.mjs [groups]` prints min/median/max gaps per prop.
- **Terrain and water are analytic and stateless.**
  - `src/terrain.js` `shore(x)` and `groundHeight(x,z)` are used by JS, by the shaders (`shoreGLSL`), by explore and game collision, and by the recorders.
  - `src/water.js` also exports CPU mirrors `sampleWater()` and `swashReach()`, which drive game buoyancy and footprints.
  - Shading-only wave detail (since 2026-10-21, same for all groups; blind scores and REPORT predate it): `swellState()` in the water fragment shader re-evaluates the four Gerstner waves per pixel (the offshore mesh is too coarse), for light through the swell (green-blue, most when backlit) and whitecaps where the crest is squeezed tightest (Jacobian), in patches, with foam left behind for a moment. The game's rowboat feeds `wakeRings` (24 stern points: x, z, time, speed; `WAKE_RINGS`): each spreads a ring of small ripples at a third of the boat's speed, which together keep the Kelvin wake's V; shading only, the surface does not move, so the CPU mirrors are unchanged.
  - Shallow water is see-through (since 2026-10-22, all groups): the water material is transparent with premultiplied alpha; up to about 1.6 m deep it writes only its own light (tint, caustics, reflection, foam) and lets the real sand and whatever stands in it (legs, the ball, a hull) through, tinted, 85% at most. Deeper it is opaque as before, except over the open-sea animals, which show through by the water's thickness in front of them (see Open sea below).
  - Wading (`src/explore.js`, game and explore alike): while the walker stands in water, the feet in turn feed `wadeRings` (10 points: x, z, time, strength; `WADE_RINGS`): short ripples (about 35 cm) running out at walking pace and a broken foam ring, gone within a couple of seconds; shading only. They replaced flat white ring meshes fixed at y 0.09.
  - All animation must derive from one time value so offline rendering is deterministic.
- **Determinism and automation hooks.** These are what the recorders and verifiers use; keep them working.
  - `window.__SCENE__` (`{scene, camera, renderer, water, …}`) and `window.__READY__`.
  - `window.__TIME__`: when set, it overrides the water/sand clock.
  - `?time=N`: freezes time.
  - With `?auto=1` only: `window.__EXPLORE__` and `window.__GAME__` (including deterministic `step(seconds)`, `teleport`, `view`, `interact`).
  - In game mode, game/explore dt is derived from the water clock, so a frozen clock freezes play. `__GAME__.step()` records the time it advanced to (`water.userData.simTime`), and the frame loop only simulates past it; before 2026-10-21 a recorder that stepped and then waited for a frame advanced play twice per step (game recordings ran at double speed).
- **Characters.** `src/game/character.js` serves both the game and the solo viewer.
  - A: procedural SkinnedMesh.
  - B: Tripo `assets/character/{idle,walk,run,jump,climb}.glb`, with clips merged onto one skeleton. Since 2026-10-20 the rig is Tripo v3.0 `spec=unity` (67 joints, three-joint fingers). It was re-rigged from the original model task with `tools/tripo_rig_test.py` and `tools/tripo_retarget_v3.py`; credits are in `assets/tripo/log.csv`. The old 41-joint rig had no fingers.
  - C: Quaternius `assets/character_C/character.glb`.
  - Missing clip poses (sit, lie, paddle, climb) are procedural bone aiming.
  - Gotcha: an `update(0)` call must not `restore()` bones. three.js `PropertyMixer` skips writing unchanged values, so the rest pose would stay on screen in offline recordings.
  - Walk/run playback is time-scaled to measured clip stride so feet don't slide.
  - IK layer (`solve()` in `character.js`, all three rigs): analytic two-bone IK for hands/feet with world targets and per-limb weights, pelvis drop for crouches, terrain-following feet (`ground`), spine lean/twist, head look-at, wrist aim (`handAim`) and finger curl (`curl`). The game passes targets per mode from `poseIK()` in `src/game/index.js`; `info().ik` reports reach errors.
  - Grip (`curl`): rigs with finger bones (B) bend each finger joint about an axis built in bind space (T pose, palms down). A rig without fingers instead gets a knuckle bone and a thumb bone per hand at load, re-skinned in bind space from vertices wholly on the hand. Wrist aim puts the roll on the forearm; a wrist that rolls far tears the skin. The Tripo climb clip is a chest-to-wall climb: at load its hips are pinned at the standing position and its hips-to-head rotations at the bind pose (values overwritten in place, since the actions already exist), so the game's body placement and `spine.lean` set the torso. On a leaning ladder `climbPose` keeps the hips about 42 cm off the ladder plane (nearly over the feet, as on steep stairs) and 25 cm below the rung line, so both knees bend. Above the top rung the hands take the handrails: `ladder.handrails` (own ladders) lists, per side, the nearest upright beside the centre line (the ladder's rails, then the posts of the railing opening), found by sideways probes; the mantle grips those posts at about waist height on the deck.
  - Launch: E at the beached boat swaps in the clone exactly where and how the prop lies (`boat.restYaw`); holding W pushes it from the stern (hands on the stern top found by scanning the centre line, lean eased where it rides high), first swinging it round on the spot if it faces up the beach, then down to the water past the umbrella and driftwood (hull corners against the prop boxes). It rests on the sand (keel on the ground) or floats, whichever is higher. Where its middle is deep enough to row (ground < -0.75 m) the rower climbs in over the stern (`boardPose()`, 3.2 s, a function of the time since it began; keys in vessel space): steps up to the stern and takes its top in both hands, pushes up with the chest folded over it (hips at the top), brings one knee then the other over (each foot on a Bézier through a point 26 cm above the top) onto what is inside (`boat.deck`: floor or thwart along the centre line, probed at hull setup), crouches with the hands on the gunwales (`boat.deck[].gun`: the side found by a ray from outside, hits over 0.9 m off the centre line skipped for C's oars), steps forward over the thwart and lowers onto it facing the bow while the hands go to the paddle. The weight presses the stern down 5° and settles the hull 2 cm. At 2.9 s the hips are on the seat and the seated pose takes over with `character.update({snapPose:true})` (body offset not blended, so no jump); `character.hipHeight` is exposed for this. With `?auto=1`, `__GAME__.boardInfo()` returns the stern, deck profile and current targets. Holding S pulls it back (0.9 m/s, walking backwards: a negative `speed` to `character.update()` runs the gait phase the other way), A / D swinging it, so a hull run into a lounger can be backed off; `verify-game` checks it. E during the push skips to the old start at the dock (the paddle, hidden while pushing, is shown again; `verify-game` checks it). With `?auto=1` it is off unless `__GAME__.pushBoat=true` (probes and recorders board directly); `__GAME__.launch` reports it. `verify-game` covers it (shot `push.png`).
  - Splashes (`src/game/splash.js`): a blade crossing the water line (in or out) and, under way, both sides of the bow emit a splash event; drops and a speckled foam ring are a pure function of the time since the event. Paddle length and roll come from the hull: at the bottom of the stroke the blade is 16 cm under the water and 45 cm clear of the side (a blade dipped beside the hull read as spray from the boat). While a blade is in the water it leaves small swirls every 0.08 s. Drops are camera-facing quads stretched along their velocity (a streak, not a bead), leaving from across the blade's width; bigger splashes add a dim mist puff; a blade just out of the water drips for 0.8 s (drip events: three falling drops and a small ring where they land). Quad winding: the side vector must be `(dir.y,-dir.x)` or the quads are back-face culled. Splash heights use `surfaceHeight()`.
  - Wake and hull foam (`src/game/wake.js`): the stern is sampled every 0.15 s while under way; the wake is a foam ribbon over those samples that widens at about the Kelvin angle (capped at 1.2 m/s), breaks up and fades over 5.5 s, and is hidden over sand. Both it and the hull foam line count as in the water only where the swash reaches (`wet()`: `z-shore(x)<swashReach(x,t)` and 10 cm deep), since the water mesh runs on over the dry beach; a boat pushed over the sand used to wear its foam line there. A foam line hugs the hull at the water line (outline probed inward at local y 0 when the hull is set up), wider at the bow under way. Foam texture is fixed to the water (v along distance travelled, the ring in world space). Everything is a function of the samples and the time, so recordings stay deterministic. `surfaceHeight()` caches the displaced grid corners per time, so the hundreds of calls per frame stay under about 0.5 ms.
  - Boat: one stroke phase drives a double-bladed paddle, both hands (overhand grip), torso twist and thrust pulses. The hull is turned so its long axis runs along travel; the rower sits on a thwart near midships, feet braced on the floor.
  - Shells: walk up, face, squat (pelvis down, feet planted), reach; the shell counts when the hand closes on it and rides in the hand.
  - Ball (since 2026-10-22): a shot, not a clip. E walks the player to 0.78 m behind the ball with the right foot in line, then IK plays `kickIK()` as a function of the time since the wind-up: the foot drawn back and up with the knee bent and the upper body leaning forward (0.3 s), the swing to the ball's lower back (the ball leaves at contact, `KICK_HIT` 0.42 s), a follow-through forward and up, back down by 0.95 s; the arms swing against the leg. With `?auto=1`, `__GAME__.kick` reports it. `explore.setHold()` blocks movement input without driving the camera.
  - Tower: `findLadder()` probes a BVH copy of the tower, in this order. The climb is a function of time, so E plays it backward to climb down.
    1. Stairs (C): tread tops rising along one direction. The climber walks the centre line; foot IK finds the treads, ignoring the handrail.
    2. The tower's own ladder (A): evenly spaced thin hits that line up. Rung heights and lean are measured, so hands and feet land on real rungs.
    3. Otherwise (B): the widest railing opening with standing room, or a railed stretch to climb over (found with vertical probes). The game draws a ladder there.
    Mantling over a railing ducks under a low roof.
  - C's shin end bone does not follow its clips. An `ankle-mark` helper on each shin tracks the animated `Foot.*` bone and serves as the leg IK effector.
  - Walk and run blend between 2.9 and 4.3 m/s on one shared stride phase, aligned at foot plants. The body's speed itself changes at a limited rate (`src/explore.js`, game and explore alike): about 0.3 s to start or stop walking, ~0.8 s from a walk up to a run or back down (a few shortening strides), ~1 s to stop from a run; with no input the last direction carries it to a stop; setHold/setDriven/clearInput stop it at once. The blend follows that speed closely (pace damping 10), and the game leans the upper body into the change (`e.accel`, ±0.1 rad via `spine.lean`). `verify-game` waits 0.9 s for the run.
  - `node scripts/probe-ik.mjs <boat|shell|tower|walk> [groups]` saves close-up stills to `shots/ik/` and logs IK errors.
- **Tide pool and open sea (game quests 5 and 6).**
  - Rock pool on the beach (`createTidePool()` in `src/game/lagoon.js`, shared by all groups; since 2026-10-22 built like the tide-pool page: its `rockGeometry()` and grain, wet/algae below a level water sheet, the seaward rocks taller to hold it on the slope) → `tidepool.html?group=<g>&embedded=1` (`src/tidepool/`) in a full-screen iframe overlay (`src/game/lagoon.js`). Gameplay: lift stones, observe 6 intertidal species. The parent polls `__TIDEPOOL__.found`.
  - Open sea (since 2026-10-20 in the beach scene, no overlay): 7 animals live around the island buoy from the start (`src/game/sea.js`), looping round it and surfacing in view of the rowboat. The quest is to observe them: from the boat, E observes the nearest unobserved animal within 30 m that is on screen with its model top at least 15 cm out of the water (`pose().showing`; the top is measured per group's model, so fin cruisers always qualify and the rest while surfacing or leaping). All 7 take about 20–35 s of waiting at the buoy. Behaviour is mostly at the surface: dorsal fins, backs rolling out with spouts, leaps and breaches, a turtle's shell. Under the water they show faintly (since 2026-10-22, all groups): `sea.js` wraps the water's `onBeforeRender` to draw the animals alone (depth-material twins carrying the swim bend) into a depth texture from the same camera; where one lies behind the water and nearer than the seabed, the water shader (`seeDepth`, off on other pages) lets it through by the water's thickness in front of it (absorption plus a fade, gone by about 3 m; weaker at grazing angles). Observing still needs the top 15 cm out. Splashes scale with the animal (since 2026-10-22, all groups; size `heft` = length/4, a humpback 2.75, a dolphin 0.65): drops (streaks, the rowboat splashes' `dropMaterial()`; a tall column for a breach), soft mist puffs over the big ones, a blow as a column of mist rising from the blowhole (a third of the body ahead of the middle) with fine drops, and `seaRings` (`SEA_RINGS` 10: x, z, time, size) in the water shader: a packet of rings running out faster and longer the bigger the splash, foam on the leading crest and a patch of white water where it went in (shading only). A back breaking the surface to breathe makes a smaller ring (`wash`). `sea.swell(x,z,t)` is the same rings as a few centimetres of lift, added to the four hull samples, so a breach nearby rocks the boat. Interactions (`seaContact()` in `src/game/index.js`): a splash or tail slap within 1.5 + 3·size m showers the boat (drops on the hull; a toast for the big ones); rowing hard (over 3 m/s) within 4 m plus a third of its length of an animal near the surface startles it: a tail slap and a dive of about a body length, back up after about 6 s (`startledAt`, 10 s cooldown; `diveDepth()`). `record-game-opensea` (DRY) still observes all 7 in A/B/C. The drop cap used to be the last frame's count, so after one frame without drops no splash showed drops again (fixed). Motion is a pure function of the water clock (`SEA` table: length, rest depth, events per cycle); paths bend around the boat. Hooks: `__GAME__.sea` (`ready`, `creatures`, `seen`, `observe(i)`, `pose(i,t)`); game state `spotted`. `node scripts/probe-sea.mjs [groups] [gpu]` → `shots/sea/`.
  - Models: A procedural (`src/game/sea-a.js`, the reef/opus lofted bodies with vertex colours), B `assets/sea/B/<id>.glb` (the Reef Lagoon's Tripo models), C `assets/sea/C/<id>.glb` (Sketchfab CC BY, `CREDITS.md`). All normalised to length 1, head +x, back +y; `SEA[i].length` sets the size for every group. A missing GLB falls back to A.
  - The old Reef Lagoon pages (`reef/opus/`, `reef/tripo_lagoon/`, `reef/codex/`) are no longer linked from the game, copied into `dist/` or `slides/live/`, or listed as slide demos (since 2026-10-20); the sources are kept unedited, and the slides still show their stills and videos.
  - The iframe is unloaded (`about:blank`) on close: two WebGL contexts blanked the beach under SwiftShader. While the overlay is open, `game.suspended` skips the beach render.
  - Tide-pool hooks: `__TIDEPOOL__` (`found`, `done`, `species`, `stones`, `group`; with `?auto=1` also `lift(i)`, `observe(id)`, `step(s)`, `project`), `__READY__`, `?time=`, `?muted=1`, `?found=`. `step(0)` freezes the iframe clock for recording.
  - Creature models follow the group: A procedural (`src/tidepool/creatures.js`), B `assets/tidepool/B/<id>.glb` (Tripo), C `assets/tidepool/C/<id>.glb` (Sketchfab/Poly Pizza, CC BY, credits in `CREDITS.md`). A missing GLB falls back to A per species.
  - GLBs are normalized with `reef/tripo/prep.py <in> <out> <preview> [tris] [rot] base`: head +X, base at y=0, longest horizontal extent 1. `species.js` `display` sets the on-screen size, shared by all groups.
- **Clipping (interactions).** `__GAME__.penetration()` (auto only) counts skinned avatar vertices (and the paddle) inside nearby props: behind the nearest face over all of a prop's meshes, with the far side of a solid, facing the other way, within 30 cm (so sitting inside a single-skin hull is not a hit); plus vertices below the sand. Up to about 3 cm is contact (a hand round a rung, thighs on a thwart).
  - Lounger: `findSurface` returns `lie {point, recline}` from the lounger's height profile (slat gaps ignored): hips just in front of the backrest bend, on a slat; `character.update({recline})` tips the body back to the backrest slope with the legs level on the seat.
  - Boat: the hull frame ignores parts sticking out (C's model includes its oars): the longest run of columns reaching near the bottom sets the centre line when it is off the box centre. The feet stand on the measured inner floor plus `character.ankleHeight`.
  - On the ground the soles keep the clip's world orientation through leg IK, so a squat does not dig the toes into the sand.
- **Islands and vegetation** (`src/coast.js` `hill()`, `src/vegetation.js`, shared by all groups; since 2026-10-21, blind scores and REPORT predate it). Reworked the same day against Codex concept art (`~/explainer-videos/beach3d-eval/island-concept/`).
  - Shape: a rounded hill, gentle at the water and rising to an off-centre summit (no cliff skirt). Bare rock is a broken band just above the water line plus the steepest faces; sand at the water; green-brown forest floor.
  - Vegetation: about 3000 small broadleaf crowns per island packed into a canopy (lumpy clumps, darker underneath, a world-space leaf-cluster pattern fading out past ~110 m, sunlit yellow-green to olive), a few emergent trees, coconut palms (shore palms leaning downhill, taller ones on the slopes standing out of the canopy), shrubs, leafy ground plants (broad-leaf rosettes and strap-leaf fans, a fringe along the forest edge spilling onto the sand and some under the canopy), and boulders along the water line (dark green weed round the foot, moss patches on top, some greener all over). Fixed seeds; instanced meshes shared by both islands (15 meshes, about 2M triangles).
  - `haze()` (exported from `vegetation.js`): island materials fade towards the fog colour past ~80 m, much more than the scene's thin fog, so the far island reads as far.
  - The terrain grid and the old blob trees used to draw from the coast's shared seed; `hill()` still draws the same numbers over the old shape, so the tide debris on the beach is unchanged (checksum of its instance matrices).
  - The sky adds about 20 small cumulus low around the horizon to the four big clouds.
  - Walking to the headland: the walk area runs along the beach to x 100, so the near island's forest edge can be reached. `coast.js` exports `islandHeight()`, `landHeight()` (beach or island, whichever is higher; used by the explore and game cameras) and `shoreClear(x,z)` (false where the island rises over 15 cm out of the sand). The headland's plants, shrubs, rocks and trunks block by their real shapes: `src/explore.js` rasterises the vegetation instances a walker on the beach can reach (inside the walk area, rooted at most 1.5 m above the sand) into the same 0.2 m cells as the props, once. Nothing grows where the island's edge runs under the beach sand, or outside its outline (boulders there used to be buried under the sand yet block walkers, or float out at sea). `verify-game` walks to it (shot `headland.png`).
- **Shadows.** The sun is low (about 22°). The shadow camera's depth range is set to the scene (near 5, far 200) with bias -.00005 and normalBias .03, map 4096: the old default range made bias -.0004 about 20 cm, so shadows started ~0.5 m from prop bases and props looked afloat.
- **Game boat in the water.** The clone floats with a draft (keel a quarter of the hull height, 12–25 cm, under the water line; height and tilt fit the water at bow, stern and both sides, since near the shore a hull levelled at its centre had water 15 cm over its inside). The heights come from `surfaceHeight()` in `src/water.js`, the water as drawn: offshore the water mesh rows are 10–16 m apart, so the flat triangles stray 20–30 cm from the exact field (`sampleWater`), and every ten seconds or so a crest covered the whole inside of a hull that followed the exact field. A depth-only cap over the hull's inside (20 cm above the water line, `renderOrder` 1, water 2) keeps the opaque water plane from showing inside the hull; the water stays at least 8 cm under it along the whole route. The hull's long axis comes from the vertex spread (C's oars skewed the box) and the narrower end is the bow (B and C ran transom first before); the rower takes a thwart clear of the floor in the aft half, so the legs have room before the bow narrows. Its materials are double-sided (C's single-skin hull showed the sea from inside).
- **Lite render on phones** (`src/lite.js`, since 2026-10-22): touch-only devices (`pointer: coarse` and no fine pointer) get pixel ratio 1, no MSAA, a 2048 shadow map, no bloom, and the islands' trees left out of the shadow map (about 6.4M → 4.3M triangles a frame, half the pixels). `?lite=1` / `?lite=0` force it. The tide-pool page takes the pixel ratio only. Desktop, stills and recordings are unchanged.
- **Bloom guard.** `src/main.js` runs a pass before bloom that turns NaN/Inf pixels to black and caps values at 1e4; otherwise one bad pixel (seen near A's palm_pair in game mode) spreads over the whole frame and the verifier sees an "empty" frame. Normal pixels are unchanged (A stills match to 1 level).
- **Collision.** The game camera uses BVH (`three-mesh-bvh`) copies of the real prop triangles. The player (`src/explore.js`) is blocked by prop geometry 0.12–1.85 m above the sand, rasterised into 0.2 m cells (body radius 0.26). Palms block only with their trunks (since 2026-10-22, all groups): `trunkOnly()` traces each trunk down from the top height band (centre follows a lean, cells within 0.3 m of it count), so the leafy plants round B's tall palm and C's pair no longer wall the walker off; those leaves (and any palm geometry below 2 m off the trunk) bend away from the walker in a vertex shader (`brushable()`, `brush` attribute, uniform at the player). Ball, boat and camera-probe collision still use the whole-prop AABBs in `colliders`.
- **Game camera and feedback** (since 2026-10-22; project skills `camera-systems` and `game-feel` in `.claude/skills/`, from awesome-gamedev-agent-skills, Apache-2.0).
  - `src/game/camera.js`: the orbit centre leads the walker in the direction of travel (0.2 s of travel, at most 0.9 m: about 0.35 m walking, 0.9 m running), eased over about 0.3 s. A jump of over 3 m between frames (a teleport, a cut between modes) is a hard cut: no lead, the camera goes straight to its spot.
  - Landing from a jump (over 0.15 s in the air): sand kicked up (`objects.puff()`: 14 grains thrown out and falling back, a soft dust sprite; a pure function of the time since it) or, where the swash reaches, a splash; the hips dip about 9 cm within 0.07 s and ease back (`poseIK()` pelvis). A kick throws sand from in front of the foot towards the ball, and the ball squashes for 0.4 s. A count going up or a quest ticking off pops in the quest book (CSS, off with reduced motion). With `?auto=1`, `__GAME__.feel` reports `landedAt`, `landSize`, `kickedAt`.
  - Gotcha: the water mesh (and `surfaceHeight()`) runs up over the dry beach, where the shader discards it beyond the swash front. To ask "is there water here", check `z-shore(x)<swashReach(x,t)` first.
- **Gait and footprints.** Walking downhill stays ground-snapped (`airborne` means a real jump). While moving, locomotion wins over one-shot poses. B/C clips are time-scaled to the measured clip speed (cap 5×). A's procedural gait matches its swing amplitude to speed. Footprints are stamped where a foot really comes down (`src/game/index.js`, since 2026-10-22): it has stopped moving across the sand (0.08 s under 0.3 m/s) near the rig's lowest foot height, and must lift (8 cm higher or over 0.8 m/s) before it prints again; a foot shuffling under 15 cm does not print twice. So stops and settling steps print under the feet. (The old code read a `character.plants` flag that never existed and printed every 0.55 m beside the body's centre.)

- Headless GPU screenshots of the tide pool occasionally capture a frame without the water layer; re-rendering the same time fixes it. The tide-pool recorders shoot each frame until two screenshots match. Also scan finished frames for single-frame spikes.

## Known weaknesses

- Water is an efficient analytical approximation, not a fluid simulation. The visible sandy bottom and caustics are evaluated inside the Water shader rather than through a refractive scene-depth buffer; submerged props will not refract correctly.
- Foam animates along a fixed shoreline; it does not physically advance over the sand. Swells are small, with planar reflection approximations.
- Landforms and canopy are procedural approximations; individual foliage clusters remain discernible. Sand and caustic patterns can reveal repetition at close range. Wet sand uses an analytical sky-colored Fresnel approximation, not a second planar reflection pass.
- Bounding-box grounding uses the slot center's ground height. Very wide future props may need per-asset adjustments to avoid local dune intersections. Animated/compressed GLB extensions have not been tested.
- SwiftShader captures prioritize reproducibility, not real-device frame-rate measurement.

## Water v2

Water and sand shading now live together in `src/water.js`, wired into `src/main.js`. The existing sun/sky, exposure, lights, camera presets, terrain functions/mesh, props/fitting, slots and Explore/compare/hub behavior are unchanged. The only time source is `water.material.uniforms.time`; the sand material references **that exact uniform object**. `?time=` and `window.__TIME__` therefore freeze/seek waves, normals, foam, caustics, swash and drying together. No simulation history, random animation state, texture downloads or wall-clock-driven shader inputs are used.

### Techniques

- Four directional Gerstner components (19, 11.3, 6.7 and 3.8 m wavelengths; offshore amplitudes 0.29, 0.16, 0.085 and 0.045 m) give actual horizontal/vertical displacement and analytical wave normals. Lagoon attenuation and a separate asymmetric shoaling bore produce readable nearshore crests. Troughs are bounded above the existing seabed to prevent disconnected water strips. Distant displacement/detail fades before coarse mesh rows can alias.
- A single coast-following water grid concentrates 35 cm rows in the surf and coarsens offshore. It contains **110,767 vertices / 220,160 triangles**, versus 204,800 triangles previously (+7.5%). The terrain itself is untouched.
- Domain-warped, world-space procedural gradient noise replaces the tiled normal texture. Four scales, with different rotations and advection directions, move independently; fine detail diminishes with viewing distance. There is no repeating normal-map tile.
- Breaking foam follows the same crest phase as the shoaling wave, with irregular caps, cellular-looking lace, small bubbles and a dispersing wake. A fast uprush and slower backwash move a conforming thin water sheet approximately 0–2.7 m onto the beach. Its ragged edge and foam coverage vary spatially. The cycle is about 4.62 s, with alongshore phase offsets.
- Sand keeps its warm hue while wetness lowers albedo/roughness. A stateless inverse-smoothstep calculation of time since retreat leaves a mottled damp mark that gradually dries. Fresnel sheen is strongest in the fresh film; the old uniform gray strip is gone.
- RGB Beer–Lambert absorption, an angle-dependent optical path, refracted procedural bottom coordinates, restrained moving caustics, shallow crest tint, Schlick Fresnel reflection and sun-aligned glitter replace the previous fixed color/reflection blend. Reflections use a bounded projected reflected ray and filtered planar samples; their sky fallback matches the existing sky gradient. The original 512×512 planar reflection pass is retained.

Wave construction was informed by [NVIDIA GPU Gems: Effective Water Simulation from Physical Models](https://developer.nvidia.com/gpugems/gpugems/part-i-natural-effects/chapter-1-effective-water-simulation-physical-models). The nearshore visual reference was [Mohamed Sameeh's Maldives surf photograph](https://unsplash.com/photos/waves-of-water-at-beach-8iKpG2BmjOA). Neither reference supplies runtime assets.

### Remaining limitations

This is an analytical lagoon approximation, not a fluid solver: breakers do not overturn into tubes or throw particle spray, and foam does not collide with individual props. Bottom refraction/caustics are procedural, so submerged models are not refracted through a scene-depth buffer. Reflections remain planar with a bounded ray approximation; steep nearshore waves and grazing views can reveal stretching, and the existing stylized clouds/landforms remain visible in reflections. Wet-sand drying is a deterministic cyclic approximation, not an accumulated physical moisture simulation. The unchanged sand tessellation can reveal minor water-film contact errors at distant/coarse shoreline sections. Real RTX profiling remains outstanding.

## Game mode

Open **http://localhost:5191/game.html** (also linked as **遊戲模式** on the hub). Defaults to **B / Tripo**; `?group=A` or `?group=C` selects another source. Press **開始玩**, finish the five tasks in any order, and return from the boat to see the completion time and **再玩一次**. A normal walk around the beach plus the approximately one-minute boat round trip is designed for a 3–5 minute visit. The automated run teleports between shore activities, so its ~1:21 simulated time is not a human playtime measurement.

### Controls and tasks

- On foot: WASD / arrows, mouse look, Shift to run, Space to jump, **E** to interact. **1 / 2 / 3** switch A/B/C without losing quests. **M** or the sound button mutes the shared ambience and game sounds. Esc releases pointer lock and pauses; **繼續玩** resumes. V switches first/third person on foot; interaction cameras return to third person. P remains Explore-only.
- Touch: left joystick moves (or steers the boat), right drag looks around on foot, yellow **互動** button performs the same action as E. Group and sound buttons remain available. The top arrow points toward the next unfinished activity and displays distance.
- **撿貝殼 ×8:** four scalloped shells and four starfish, at deterministic sand/shallow-water locations outside conservative slot envelopes. Gold rings identify collectibles, including submerged ones. Pickup hops, pooled sparkles and a soft chime provide feedback.
- **踢沙灘球:** approach from the landward side and press E to kick away from the character. The striped ball has gravity, bounce, rolling drag, prop AABB and player collision, and buoyancy sampled from the water field. Crossing into water deeper than 0.65 m finishes the task.
- **躺椅休息:** interact beside the umbrella. A/B use a raycast-selected surface of a real lounger in the umbrella model, with the long axis and raised backrest determining the reclining direction. C has no lounger and sits on the sand under its umbrella. Skeleton poses ease in over approximately 0.4 seconds. Rest for 1.2 seconds; E stands up.
- **爬上救生塔看海:** interact at the tower approach. A short 1.1-second ascent follows the ladder side to a raycast-selected deck point, preferring standing clearance below/alongside the roof. No extra plank or support posts are added. Stay for 1.2 seconds; E returns to the approach point. A missing tower degrades to the grounded lookout location.
- **划小船到外海小島:** E at the beached boat launches it into sufficiently deep water. W/S paddle forward/backward; A/D steer. Follow the gold buoy near the offshore island `(60, -286)`, then follow the returning arrow to the launch ring. E disembarks only within 11 m of that ring; the quest finishes only after the island visit **and** return/disembark. Shallows, prop bounds, and the existing island footprints block sailing through land. Waves control heave, pitch and roll; paddle sounds reuse the ambience's AudioContext and master gain.
- **留下腳印:** a passive bonus, not a completion prerequisite. Up to 128 instanced sole marks fade over 20 seconds; the shared swash field accelerates washing to about half a second after contact.

### Architecture and boundaries

- `game.html` shares `src/main.js`'s scene, renderer, lighting and postprocessing. The game module loads only on that pathname. It is a fifth Vite build entry. Hub navigation is the only existing page UI addition.
- `src/game/index.js` owns quest state, start/replay/completion, interaction targets, camera modes and rowing. The small optional adapter in `src/explore.js` exposes the existing avatar, inputs, start gesture, shared audio, and a movement/camera override. Ordinary Explore and comparison keep their original defaults.
- `src/game/objects.js` owns instanced shells/starfish, collection rings, 48 pooled sparkle instances, 128 instanced footprint decals, and the beach ball. `physics.js` substeps the ball at at most 1/60 s. Reusable vectors, wave-output records, interaction records and pooled instances avoid allocating geometry or physics objects in the animation loop. Sound nodes are short-lived interaction/paddle events and disconnect when finished.
- `sampleWater(x,z,time,out)` and `swashReach(x,time)` are additive exports from `src/water.js`. They mirror the existing four Gerstner components, attenuation, coastal bore/noise, seabed clamp and shore film; the sampler inverts horizontal displacement and derives the local surface slope. Shader strings, water mesh, shading and material settings are unchanged. Ball/boat queries and visual effects use `water.material.uniforms.time`, and the footprint shader shares that exact uniform object. `?time=` and `window.__TIME__` continue to freeze/seek the water. Game input/physics use nonnegative, bounded differences of that clock rather than a second animation clock.
- Quests anchor to config slots and current bounding boxes. Sailing uses a detached clone sharing the selected source model's geometry/materials, temporarily hiding the beached source instance; disembarking restores it. A cached procedural hull is used when the GLB is unavailable. The boat seat is sampled from the clone's actual geometry; chairs and tower decks are exclusively source geometry. Source models, fitting rules, `assets/props.json`, terrain shape, coast geometry, camera presets and recording/shooting scripts were not edited.
- Only `?auto=1` exposes `window.__GAME__`: read-only state snapshots, target locations, on-foot teleport, view/steering helpers, `interact()`, deterministic `step(seconds)`, and live vessel state. It has no quest-completion setter; automated completion uses the same interaction and physics paths as play.

Game camera obstruction uses five near-plane rays against double-sided BVH-indexed copies of the actual prop triangles (separate collision geometry, no source edits), with AABBs used only for broad-phase rejection. Small game objects and the avatar are excluded. The existing opaque water shader hides submerged shell geometry, so surface rings identify those pickups.

- **陰影與物件接地、小船吃水（2026-10-21）**：陰影相機的深度範圍改成貼合場景（near 5、far 200），偏移改為約 1 cm 並加法線偏移、陰影圖 4096。原本偏移在 500 m 的預設深度範圍下約 20 cm，太陽仰角只有 22°，影子從物件底部約 0.5 m 外才開始，看起來像浮在沙上。物件擺放三組共用新規則：最底部 6 cm 頂點到沙面的距離中位數為 0，貼著斜坡坐下（`scripts/probe-ground.mjs` 量測）。遊戲小船改成吃水 12–25 cm（原本整個船底架在水面上），船艙內加一片只寫深度的遮罩，水面不會畫進船裡。船的高度與傾斜改由船頭、船尾、兩側四點的水面決定（原本只看船中央一點，靠岸浪短時船艙邊緣的水會高出遮罩 10–15 cm），遮罩提高到水線上 20 cm，整段航程水面都至少低於遮罩 8 cm；C 組船身改用頂點分布找長軸（原本被自帶的槳拉歪約 30°），船殼改雙面繪製（原本從船艙往下看會看穿到水）。固定鏡頭截圖已重拍；盲評分數與 REPORT 的數字是之前的畫面。
- **划船水花（2026-10-21）**：槳葉入水、出水各濺一次水花（水滴＋擴散的泡沫圈），船速超過 1.2 m/s 時船頭兩側持續濺起小浪花；每個水花是一個事件，水滴位置只由事件後經過的時間決定，逐格錄影結果一致（`src/game/splash.js`）。原本槳的傾斜角上限 0.55 rad，槳葉最低仍離水面約 17 cm，從來沒入水；上限改為 0.95 rad，現在槳葉會入水約 15 cm。
- **划槳位置、船頭方向、外海水面進船（2026-10-21）**：槳葉原本只在船邊 0.7–0.8 m 入水（B 組船寬一半約 0.65 m），水花貼著船身，看起來像船濺起來的；槳長和傾斜改依船寬推算，划到最低時槳葉在水下 16 cm、離船側 45 cm，在水裡時每 0.08 秒留下一個小槳渦。B、C 組原本是船尾朝前倒著走（找長軸時只定了軸、沒定方向），改成較窄的一端當船頭；座位改選船艙後半、高於底板的座板，腳不會伸進變窄的船頭。外海水面網格的列距有 10–16 m，畫出來的水面和精確波形可差 20–30 cm，約每 10 秒會有一兩格整個船艙被水蓋住；新增 `surfaceHeight()` 依網格內插算「畫出來的水面」，船和水花都改用它，逐像素比對三組都只剩水線以下的船底被水遮住。
- **推船下水（2026-10-21）**：在沙灘上的小船按 E，不再淡出直接傳送到離岸 9 m 的船上；船會從原本擺放的位置和角度開始，按住 W 從船尾推（手扶船尾上緣），船頭朝陸地的會先原地轉向，再沿著避開陽傘和漂流木的路線推下沙灘、涉水，水深到可以划（船中央地面低於 −0.75 m）時從船尾爬上船，三組約 14 秒。推的時候人腳和船頭在水裡會濺水花。A / D 微調方向，E 跳過直接上船。自動化模式（`?auto=1`）預設直接上船，`__GAME__.pushBoat=true` 才走推船流程，`verify-game` 有測。
- **船尾航跡與吃水線泡沫（2026-10-21）**：參考一般遊戲做法（CapCôtier 的泡沫帶、Tidewater／Boat Attack 的航跡圖），新增 `src/game/wake.js`。划船時每 0.15 秒記下船尾位置，畫成一條貼在水面上的泡沫帶：兩側是船頭浪散開的兩條泡沫線，中間是划槳攪出的白沫，約以開爾文角（19.5°）往外張開（最快每秒 1.2 m），5.5 秒內碎成小塊後消失，碰到沙灘的部分不畫。船身吃水線一圈泡沫，船速越快船頭越寬。泡沫貼圖固定在水面上，不跟著船滑動。全部由取樣與時間算出，逐格錄影一致。`surfaceHeight()` 改為同一時間共用網格頂點的計算結果，每格多約 0.5 ms。前後對照：`video/wake_before_after.mp4`。
- **水花水滴改版（2026-10-21）**：水滴從小圓球改成面向鏡頭、沿速度方向拉長的半透明貼片（看起來像飛濺的水痕），從槳葉整個寬度噴出；用力入水時多一團淡淡往上散的水霧；槳葉出水後 0.8 秒內一路滴水，落水處留下小水圈；小槳渦只帶幾顆水滴。水滴核心亮度調低，避免剛濺起時疊在一起被泛光放大成白球。
- **海浪細節（2026-10-21）**：只改水面著色，不動水面幾何，CPU 的 `sampleWater()`／`surfaceHeight()` 不變。外海網格太粗，所以在 fragment shader 逐像素重算 4 道 Gerstner 波（`swellState()`）：浪體上半部透出綠藍色的光（逆光時最明顯），浪峰被擠得最尖的地方冒出白浪（看水平位移的 Jacobian，分塊出現，碎後留一點白沫）。這片海浪小，白浪很少，比較像平靜的潟湖。遊戲中小船把最近 24 個船尾位置傳給水面（`wakeRings`），每點以船速三分之一往外擴散一圈小波紋，疊起來形成約 19.5° 的 V 形尾流（運動學尾流的做法）；從上往下看反射很弱，所以波紋面向鏡頭的一側稍亮、背向的稍暗。三組共用，盲評分數與 REPORT 是之前的畫面。`verify-explore` 在機器高負載時手機頁面 30 秒內載不完會逾時，改動前的版本也一樣。
- **小島植被（2026-10-21）**：原本兩座島（遠處小島與右側岬角）各是 3200 顆圓球樹冠，看起來一團團。改成 `src/vegetation.js`：闊葉樹冠由幾顆變形的小球拼成不規則的一團、底部與內側較暗、近看有葉叢明暗（shader 的世界座標雜訊，約 110 m 外淡出避免閃爍），下面有短樹幹，少數高大的突出樹讓輪廓起伏；椰子樹（彎曲漸細的樹幹、下垂的羽狀葉、底下幾顆椰子）多長在靠海處、往下坡傾；林緣、低處與岩坡有灌木。地面顏色：林下改淺一點的綠褐色（原本樹冠間的縫是黑的），水邊一圈沙與濕岩，岩石調亮。全部固定種子，兩座島共用 9 個 InstancedMesh。原本樹木的亂數和海灘碎貝殼共用同一個種子，所以 `hill()` 照舊抽同樣的亂數，碎貝殼位置不變（實例矩陣校驗和相同）。wide 鏡頭：draw call 63 → 83，三角形 338 萬 → 395 萬（含陰影與反射 pass）。三組共用，盲評分數與 REPORT 是之前的畫面。
- **爬進小船（2026-10-21）**：推船到水夠深之後，原本是 1.2 秒從身後直線內插到座位、中間往上跳一下，身體直接轉正，看起來像飄進船裡。現在是 3.2 秒的分段動作（全部由經過的時間決定，逐格錄影一致）：走近船尾、雙手抓住船尾上緣 → 撐起身體、胸口趴過船尾（臀部到船尾頂的高度）→ 一隻膝蓋跨過船尾、踩到船裡（地板或座板），另一隻再跨進來 → 蹲低、雙手改扶兩側船舷 → 往前跨過座板 → 面向船頭坐下，手移到槳上。船內可以踩的高度（`boat.deck`）和船舷位置在設定船的時候量好：船舷用從船外往內打的射線找（C 組自帶的槳會把外框撐寬到 3.5 m，超過中線 0.9 m 的命中略過；單層船殼從裡面打會打不到）。爬進來時船尾被壓低約 5°、整條船下沉 2 cm。臀部到座位時（2.9 秒）切換成坐姿並跳過姿勢過渡（`snapPose`），身體不會彈一下。量測：手到目標的誤差多數 ≤ 0.12 m，蹲在船裡扶船舷時最多 0.28 m（C 組）；B 組跨過船尾那一下小腿陷入船尾約 11 cm、從座板踩下時腳趾約 9 cm，坐下後轉成划船姿勢的 0.3 秒內大腿碰座板約 13 cm（舊版上船後也一樣）。
- **走跑切換加減速（2026-10-21）**：原本角色速度在一格內就從 4.5 m/s 變成 1.8 m/s 或 0，動畫混合再追上去，所以放開 Shift 時像慢動作跑步，停下時整個人定格、腿停在半空再變回站姿。現在速度本身有加減速：起步與從走路停下約 0.3 秒，走↔跑約 0.8 秒（幾步漸短的步幅），從跑步停下約 1 秒；沒有輸入時沿最後的方向減速停下。遊戲中上半身依加速度前傾或後仰（最多約 6°）。混合權重改為緊跟實際速度，步頻仍依實際速度推算，腳不滑。
- **錄影時遊戲跑兩倍速（2026-10-21 修正）**：`__GAME__.step(dt)` 推進時鐘並更新遊戲後，`main.js` 的畫面迴圈用「水面時鐘－上次畫面時間」又更新一次，所以「step 後等畫面」的錄影腳本（外海、遊戲精華、遊戲潮池、走位）裡角色、小船、划槳都是兩倍速。現在 `step()` 記下已推進到的時間（`water.userData.simTime`），畫面迴圈只補算之後的部分。外海錄影模擬三組仍觀察到 7 種、`verify-game` 通過。
- **小島外形與植被對照意象圖（2026-10-21）**：用 Codex 只看文字描述畫了三張意象圖（沙灘遠景、海上看遠島、俯瞰岬角，`~/explainer-videos/beach3d-eval/island-concept/`），跟現況對照，差最多的是外形與植被尺度：原本是平頂、四周一圈黑色岩壁、樹冠又大又少（像長滿花椰菜的平台）。修改：`hill()` 改成圓丘（水邊平緩、往偏離中心的山頂升高），岩石只留水邊一圈斷續的濕岩帶和最陡的坡面；樹冠改小、數量約 4 倍（每島約 3000 顆）並墊高成一層林冠，顏色提亮成向光的黃綠到橄欖綠，少數深色；坡上的椰子樹加高到冒出林冠，岸邊椰子樹往海傾；水邊散落岩塊；島的材質過了約 80 m 往霧色淡出（`haze()`），遠島看起來比較遠；天空多約 20 朵靠近地平線的小積雲。碎貝殼位置不變（校驗和相同）。植被三角形 64 萬 → 187 萬，wide 鏡頭 GPU 每幀約 1.09 → 1.20 ms。還沒做的：淺水珊瑚暗影、林緣灌木伸到沙上。三組共用，盲評分數與 REPORT 是之前的畫面。
- **小島林緣植物與綠礁石（2026-10-22）**：島上原本只有椰子樹、球狀樹冠和灌木，沒有一般的植物；水邊岩塊是單純的灰石頭。加了大葉的地被植物（闊葉蓮座：拱起的葉柄、寬葉，類似海葡萄、姑婆芋；細長的帶狀葉扇形展開，類似林投幼株），沿林緣長成一圈、伸到沙上，林下空隙與岩石間也有一些（近島 1300、遠島 900 株）。岩塊底部加一圈深綠色海藻（水打濕的位置），頂上有苔斑，約四分之一整顆偏綠。三組共用。
- **走到岬角近看、推船可以往回拉（2026-10-22）**：走路範圍原本到 x 35 為止，右側岬角（近島）走不到。現在沙灘一路走到 x 100，可以走到岬角的林緣，站在岩塊、大葉植物和椰子樹旁邊；島坡從沙裡升起超過 15 cm 的地方、椰子樹幹與岩塊會擋人，所以進不了林子。鏡頭碰撞也把島坡算進去。順帶修正：水邊岩塊原本在島外框外面也會取樣（那裡高度固定 −0.5），有的埋在海灘沙底下還會擋人，有的散在外海浮在水上；現在只放在島的範圍內、且不放在被沙蓋住的地方（地被植物、椰子樹同）。推船時原本只能按 W 往前推，船撞到躺椅或洋傘就卡住；現在按住 S 會倒退著把船往回拉（約 0.9 m/s，腳步動畫倒著播），拉的同時按 A/D 可轉向，提示改成「按住 W 把船推進水深處 · S 往回拉」。`verify-game` 加了往回拉與走到岬角兩項檢查。
- **林緣碰撞、淺水透明與涉水漣漪（2026-10-22）**：林緣原本只有椰子樹幹和岩塊用圓形近似擋人，灌木和大葉植物會被穿過去。現在把走得到範圍內的植被實例（灌木、地被植物、岩塊、樹幹）用實際三角形畫進跟道具同一張 0.2 m 碰撞格，0.12–1.85 m 高的部分會擋人。水面原本完全不透明，淺水下的沙是 shader 算出來的，腳一進水就看不見；現在水面改成半透明（premultiplied alpha），約 1.6 m 深以內透出真正的沙地與泡在水裡的腳、球、船身，帶水色，最多透 85%；更深維持不透明。原本涉水時每 0.22 秒在身體中心放一圈固定在 y=0.09 的白色細環，看起來很假；改成兩腳輪流在水面 shader 產生約 35 cm 波長的細小漣漪，加一圈破碎的泡沫，兩秒內消失（`wadeRings`，只改著色）。三組共用。
- **腳印位置（2026-10-22）**：原本程式檢查 `character.plants` 決定用動畫的踩地時間點蓋腳印，但這個屬性從來不存在，所以一直走備用方案：每走 0.55 m 在身體中心左右 13 cm 交替蓋一個，跟實際的腳對不上，停下來時最後一隻腳的腳印落後約 0.8 m（B 組停步時還會在 0.13 秒內亂蓋三個）。現在依腳的實際位置判斷：腳在沙上停住（0.3 m/s 以下持續 0.08 秒）且接近這組角色腳的最低高度才蓋，抬起 8 cm 以上或速度超過 0.8 m/s 才能再蓋下一個，移動不到 15 cm 的小挪步不重複蓋。三組停下來時最後兩個腳印都在腳底下（差 1 cm 內）。
- **鏡頭往前看、瞬移直接切、落地與踢球回饋（2026-10-22）**：參考 `camera-systems`、`game-feel` 兩個 skill。跑步時鏡頭的環繞中心往前進方向超前（走路約 0.35 m、跑步 0.9 m，約 0.3 秒慢慢移過去），看得到前面；一格內移動超過 3 m（傳送、切換模式）時鏡頭直接切到定位，不從遠處滑過來。跳躍落地揚起沙粒和淡淡沙塵（在浪打得到的地方改成水花），膝蓋緩衝讓臀部下沉約 9 cm 再回來；踢球時腳前揚沙、球被踢扁 0.4 秒再彈回；任務清單的數字增加或打勾時彈一下（減少動態設定下關閉）。順帶修正：水面網格延伸到乾沙灘上（shader 在浪打不到的地方丟掉），所以在乾沙上量到的水面高度比地面高，涉水漣漪和落地判斷會誤以為在水裡；改成先檢查浪有沒有打到。
# 3D 場景驗證流程手冊（下次換主題照做）

beach3d-eval 實際跑過的流程、指令與踩過的坑。換主題（森林、城市、室內…）時，複製整個專案，改 `assets/props.json` 與底座 brief 即可沿用。

## 實測耗時與花費（海邊、8 件物件）

| 步驟 | 耗時 | 花費 |
|---|---|---|
| 底座：水、天空、沙灘、光線（codex 2 輪） | 6.8 分 | 約 186 萬 token |
| A 組：codex 程序化物件 | 6.7 分 | 約 150 萬 token |
| B 組：Tripo 生成 8 件（逐件跑）＋ Blender 減面 | 18.5 分＋2 分 | 140 點（另試生成 130 點） |
| C 組：素材庫挑選＋匯入（Blender MCP） | 4.8 分 | 0（CC BY 需標作者） |
| 遊覽模式＋入口頁＋並排比較（codex） | 8.1 分 | 約 215 萬 token |
| 水面升級 Water v2（codex，high 推理） | 30 分（含軟體算繪影片約 15 分） | codex 額度 |
| codex 盲評 3 輪 | 約 20 秒 | 少量 token |
| 60 秒影片（逐格算繪＋合成） | 約 3 分 | 0 |

## 流程

### 0. 開專案
- 系統 Python 沒有 ensurepip，venv 用 uv 建：`uv venv && uv pip install tripo3d`
- Vite 開發伺服器**自己在背景開**：`npx vite --port 5191 --strictPort`。brief 裡要寫明「伺服器已在跑，不要另開」。codex 開的伺服器會隨 codex 結束一起被關掉。
- `.env` 放 `TRIPO_API_KEY`（chmod 600、gitignore），由使用者手動填，不要貼進對話。

### 1. 規劃 `assets/props.json`
- `cameras`：固定截圖鏡頭（wide／beach／closeup）。
- `slots`：每件物件都有 `id`、`pos`、`height`，選填 `maxLen`，以及英文 `prompt`。A／B／C 三組共用同一份 prompt。
- **縮放規則三組一致**：`scale = min(height/size.y, maxLen/max(size.x,size.z))`。只用高度縮放的話，長形物件（船、漂流木）會變得巨大，所以長形物件一定要設 `maxLen`。

### 2. 底座與 A 組（codex）
- 寫 `BRIEF_*.md`（任務、不能動的部分、驗證方式），再跑 `tools/codex_run.sh <組別> <步驟> <brief>`。
  - 腳本內容：用 `timed.sh` 計時，執行 `codex exec --json -s workspace-write -c sandbox_workspace_write.network_access=true -c service_tier='"fast"' -o logs/<步驟>.last.md`，prompt 從 stdin 餵入。
- token 用量會從 `logs/<步驟>.jsonl` 最後一筆 usage 抓出來（`build_stats.py`）。
- 底座的已知弱點是植被呈圓球狀、雲很卡通，物件來源幫不上忙。下次可以考慮 HDRI 天空，或用 Tripo 生成植被。
- 水面請直接沿用 `src/water.js`（Water v2：Gerstner 波浪、不重複法線、沖岸泡沫、濕沙）。第一版的格子紋、虛線泡沫、灰色濕沙帶都已解決，brief 見 `BRIEF_water.md`。
- codex 沙箱用不到 GPU，會退回 swiftshader，每格約 1.5 秒。長影片改由我們自己用 GPU 算繪，brief 裡請 codex 只跑 2fps 預覽就好。
- 所有動畫都只能由 time uniform（`window.__TIME__`）驅動，逐格算繪才會穩定。

### 3. B 組（Tripo）
- `.venv/bin/python tools/tripo_gen.py --dry-run`：先列清單，**使用者確認後才花點數**。
- 模型版本以 API 實際接受的為準，SDK docstring 列的不一定能用。可用版本：`P1-20260311`、`P2-20260801`、`v2.5-20250123`、`v3.0-20250812`、`v3.1-20260211`。
- **選 v3.1**：每件 20 點，約 2–3 分鐘，產出約 147 萬面、品質最好。P2 每件 110 點、只有 4.3k 面，反而比較醜。
- 下載前輸出資料夾必須先存在，腳本已修好。下載失敗不用重新生成：用 `client.get_usage()` 找 task id，再跑 `tools/tripo_gen.py --recover <task_id> <slot>`。
- 減面（必做，原始模型網頁跑不動）：`tools/decimate_all.sh [30000]`，每件約 15 秒，用 Blender 無頭模式 COLLAPSE 減面，匯出貼圖用 JPEG。
- 可改進：8 件同時送出，生成時間可從 18.5 分縮到 5 分以內。

### 4. C 組（免費素材庫，Blender MCP）
- Blender 5.2.1 位置：`~/.local/opt/blender-5.2.1-linux-x64/blender`，Cycles 已設定 OPTIX。
- MCP 的素材庫開關是**每個 scene 各自一份**。新建 scene 後，要把 `blendermcp_use_polyhaven` 等屬性從 'Scene' 複製過去。
- 匯入後檢查：
  - 多出來的 Icosphere 要刪掉。
  - 帶 armature 的模型匯出 GLB 後零件會跑位，直接換別的模型。
  - 作者寫進 `assets/library/CREDITS.md`。
- 素材庫最大的問題是**找不到符合需求的模型**（茅草屋、草編傘＋躺椅），只能將就。

### 5. 截圖與對照圖
- `node scripts/shoot.mjs <A|B|C>`：三個固定鏡頭，輸出 `shots/<組>/*.png`。
- `node scripts/shoot-props.mjs <組> [slot]`：單件物件展示圖。
- `python3 tools/compare.py`：輸出 `compare/<鏡頭>.png`，三欄並排並標註耗時與花費。
- `python3 tools/build_stats.py`：輸出 `report/stats.json`，入口頁會讀取這份資料。
- 單張截圖用 swiftshader 就夠（約 1.6 秒一張）。

### 6. 可遊覽介面（codex）
- `BRIEF_explore.md`：遊覽模式，WASD 移動、1/2/3 切換組別、V 切換第一和第三人稱、P 拍照。
- `BRIEF_compare.md`：入口頁、三欄同步比較、單件模型檢視。
- 網址：`/`、`/compare.html?groups=A,B,C`、`/scene.html?explore=1&group=B`、`/props.html?group=B`

### 7. codex 盲評
- `python3 tools/blind_score.py [輪數]`
  - 三組匿名成 X／Y／Z，每輪輪換順序。
  - 附 3 張場景圖和物件總表，用 `-i` 附圖、prompt 走 stdin、`-s read-only`。
  - 輸出 `eval/scores.json`，會還原成原本組別再平均。
- 評分項目：符合需求、物件質感、整體協調、第一眼觀感，再加上每件物件各自的分數。
- 截圖上不能有組別文字，跑之前先確認。

### 8. 60 秒對照影片
1. 編輯 `video/path.json`：鏡頭關鍵格（`t`、`pos`、`target`，以 Catmull-Rom 曲線串接）和每段說明（`from`、`to`、`title`、`text`、`slots`）。
2. **先跑低格率預覽**，確認鏡頭沒有穿進物件：`node scripts/record-path.mjs B 0.5`，再把影格拼成縮圖總表檢查。這次就抓到鏡頭穿過陽傘和小船。
3. 正式算繪：三組平行跑 `node scripts/record-path.mjs A|B|C`，約 2.5 分鐘。
   - 用 GPU：`--use-gl=angle --use-angle=gl-egl`，每格 0.17 秒，比 swiftshader 快 10 倍。
   - 頁面透過 `window.__TIME__` 固定水面時間，所以三組逐格完全對齊。
4. `python3 tools/make_video.py`：片頭、四宮格（A、B、C 加說明格）、結論表，輸出 `video/compare.mp4`，約 30 秒完成。

## 換主題時要改的地方
- `assets/props.json`：鏡頭、物件槽位、prompt。
- 底座 brief（地形、水、天空、光線），以及 `src/main.js` 和 `src/terrain.js`。
- `video/path.json`：關鍵格座標要依新的物件位置重排。
- `tools/make_video.py`：片頭和結論文字、`NAMES` 對照表。
- `tools/build_stats.py`：notes 文字。

## 換模型比較（2026-10-19）
同一份需求、同一套流程（底座 → 第二輪意見 → A 組物件 → 水面），各自在獨立 worktree 從 commit 8c15a75 開始跑：

| 版本 | 設定 | 總耗時 | 花費 | codex 盲評 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| codex 第一輪（beach3d-eval） | 沙箱、推理 low（水面 high） | 44 分 | 約 1,176 萬 token | 7.1 |
| codex 第二輪（beach3d-codex2） | `-s danger-full-access`、fast、推理 high | 33 分 | 約 990 萬 token | 7.9 |
| Opus 5.5（beach3d-opus） | `tools/claude_run.sh`（claude -p，隔離 MCP 與設定） | 119 分 | API 換算 26.35 美元 | 8.6 |

- 盲評：`BLIND_CONFIG='{"groups":{...},"out":"eval_models","intro":"..."}' python3 tools/blind_score.py 3`
- 對照圖與水面影片：`python3 tools/compare_models.py`（先用 record-path.mjs + video/water16.json 錄三個版本；別的 port 用 `SCENE_URL`、需要等待用 `SETTLE_MS`）
- codex 結束時 vite 會被一起關掉，錄影前要自己重開。
- 錄影發現 Opus 版約 30% 畫格全黑：茅草材質 alpha test＋bump map 產生 NaN。給 Opus 一輪修 bug（6.6 分、1.03 美元）後只剩 1 格。brief 裡應附錄影器讓模型自己跑飛越檢查。

- Walking to the headland: the walk area runs along the beach to x 100, so the near island's forest edge can be reached. `coast.js` exports `islandHeight()`, `landHeight()` (beach or island, whichever is higher; used by the explore and game cameras) and `shoreClear(x,z)` (false where the island rises over 15 cm out of the sand). The headland's plants, shrubs, rocks and trunks block by their real shapes: `src/explore.js` rasterises the vegetation instances a walker on the beach can reach (inside the walk area, rooted at most 1.5 m above the sand) into the same 0.2 m cells as the props, once. Nothing grows where the island's edge runs under the beach sand, or outside its outline (boulders there used to be buried under the sand yet block walkers, or float out at sea). `verify-game` walks to it (shot `headland.png`).
- **Shadows.** The sun is low (about 22°). The shadow camera's depth range is set to the scene (near 5, far 200) with bias -.00005 and normalBias .03, map 4096: the old default range made bias -.0004 about 20 cm, so shadows started ~0.5 m from prop bases and props looked afloat.
- **Game boat in the water.** The clone floats with a draft (keel a quarter of the hull height, 12–25 cm, under the water line; height and tilt fit the water at bow, stern and both sides, since near the shore a hull levelled at its centre had water 15 cm over its inside). The heights come from `surfaceHeight()` in `src/water.js`, the water as drawn: offshore the water mesh rows are 10–16 m apart, so the flat triangles stray 20–30 cm from the exact field (`sampleWater`), and every ten seconds or so a crest covered the whole inside of a hull that followed the exact field. A depth-only cap over the hull's inside (20 cm above the water line, `renderOrder` 1, water 2) keeps the opaque water plane from showing inside the hull; the water stays at least 8 cm under it along the whole route. The hull's long axis comes from the vertex spread (C's oars skewed the box) and the narrower end is the bow (B and C ran transom first before); the rower takes a thwart clear of the floor in the aft half, so the legs have room before the bow narrows. Its materials are double-sided (C's single-skin hull showed the sea from inside).
- **Lite render on phones** (`src/lite.js`, since 2026-10-22): touch-only devices (`pointer: coarse` and no fine pointer) get pixel ratio 1, no MSAA, a 2048 shadow map, no bloom, and the islands' trees left out of the shadow map (about 6.4M → 4.3M triangles a frame, half the pixels). `?lite=1` / `?lite=0` force it. The tide-pool page takes the pixel ratio only. Desktop, stills and recordings are unchanged.
- **Bloom guard.** `src/main.js` runs a pass before bloom that turns NaN/Inf pixels to black and caps values at 1e4; otherwise one bad pixel (seen near A's palm_pair in game mode) spreads over the whole frame and the verifier sees an "empty" frame. Normal pixels are unchanged (A stills match to 1 level).
- **Collision.** The game camera uses BVH (`three-mesh-bvh`) copies of the real prop triangles. The player (`src/explore.js`) is blocked by prop geometry 0.12–1.85 m above the sand, rasterised into 0.2 m cells (body radius 0.26). Palms block only with their trunks (since 2026-10-22, all groups): `trunkOnly()` traces each trunk down from the top height band (centre follows a lean, cells within 0.3 m of it count), so the leafy plants round B's tall palm and C's pair no longer wall the walker off; those leaves (and any palm geometry below 2 m off the trunk) bend away from the walker in a vertex shader (`brushable()`, `brush` attribute, uniform at the player). Ball, boat and camera-probe collision still use the whole-prop AABBs in `colliders`.

A jump of over 3 m between frames (a teleport, a cut between modes) is a hard cut: no lead, the camera goes straight to its spot.

A kick throws sand from in front of the foot towards the ball, and the ball squashes for 0.4 s. A count going up or a quest ticking off pops in the quest book (CSS, off with reduced motion). With `?auto=1`, `__GAME__.feel` reports `landedAt`, `landSize`, `kickedAt`.

# Tropical cove — shared A/B/C base

Run with Node 22:

```sh
npm ci --cache /tmp/beach-npm-cache
npx vite --port 5191 --strictPort
node scripts/shoot.mjs A
```

Open `http://localhost:5191/?group=A&cam=wide`. Fixed views are `wide`, `beach`, and `closeup`; omit `cam` for mouse/touch OrbitControls. `?time=4` freezes water animation for repeatable comparisons. All screenshot runs use the same time, 1280×720 viewport, specified Chromium executable, and SwiftShader flags.

## Built

- Three.js Water with planar reflections, locally generated repeating normal map, animated fine normals and small geometric swells, sun specular glitter, depth-based turquoise-to-blue absorption, procedural seabed ripples and animated caustics, and broken shoreline foam.
- A shared analytical shoreline controls terrain, wet sand, foam and water depth. Sand has dune relief, a raised berm, filtered wind-ripple normals, and a roughly three-metre dark, low-roughness wet band with an analytical sky-reflection tint. Seeded shells, pebbles and seaweed follow the high-tide debris line. Rocky ridges, dark canopy and a right-hand headland belong to the shared landscape, outside the prop slots.
- Procedural tropical-blue sky with soft cumulus, warm afternoon directional sunlight and hemisphere fill, ACES tone mapping, restrained bloom, atmospheric haze, and shadow support for future props.
- Eight empty `THREE.Group` markers preserve each slot's exact id and position. `src/props.js` exports `loadProps(group)`, `propRoot`, and one empty A function per slot in `slotStubs`.
- B/C use `slot.paths.B` / `slot.paths.C` in `assets/props.json`, load with GLTFLoader, normalize bounding-box height, center X/Z, and place the minimum Y at the analytical ground height. Paths point to `assets/tripo/<id>.glb` and `assets/library/<id>.glb`.
- Vite production builds copy the assets directory, including future GLBs, into `dist/assets`.

## Visual iterations

Four wide-view checkpoints record three screenshot → correction → screenshot cycles. All use the original camera coordinates and frozen time 4.

| Checkpoint | Review and subsequent fixes |
| --- | --- |
| `shots/base_r1.png` | Excessive terrain ridge, beach camera below sand, washed-out water. Capped shoreline curvature, lowered dunes, reduced reflection/light contribution. |
| `shots/base_r2.png` | Broad bloom washed out the coast; uniform foam; regular sand ripples. Reduced bloom and bounded reflected radiance, broke up foam, varied ripples and filtered the normal map. |
| `shots/base_r3.png` | Far terrain boundary visible, water too flat, sand too gray-green. Extended terrain with a nonuniform grid, added small swells and fine wave normals, warmed sand and lighting. |
| `shots/base_r4.png` | Final shared base. Distant boundary removed, turquoise depth gradient readable, warmer sand. |

Final camera images: `shots/A/wide.png`, `shots/A/beach.png`, `shots/A/closeup.png`. Props deliberately remain absent, so the fixed closeup is mostly empty sand until later groups are implemented.

## Shared base polish — round 2

Three additional screenshot → review → fix rounds used the unchanged wide and beach cameras, 1280×720 and frozen time 4. Each checkpoint also has a corresponding `shots/base2_rN_beach.png`.

| Checkpoint | Review and subsequent fixes |
| --- | --- |
| `shots/base2_r1.png` | Added dunes/berm, wet band and tide debris, rolling breakers, blue sky, ridged island and right headland. Ripples were too strong and canopy too spherical/dark; reduced and distance-filtered ripple normals, shrank and increased canopy clusters, broke up foam lines. |
| `shots/base2_r2.png` | Sand relief became subtler and surf readable. Sun glare was excessive, foliage material multiplied its instance colors too dark, and clouds were stretched; bounded glitter, corrected canopy color multiplication and replaced cloud patches with rounded cumulus. |
| `shots/base2_r3.png` | Clouds were oversized and canopy still too coarse. Reduced cloud size, increased smaller canopy clusters, warmed wet sand, increased water-normal frequency for finer mid-distance detail and tightened visible glitter. |
| `shots/A/{wide,beach,closeup}.png` | Final captures after the third correction, regenerated with the original `node scripts/shoot.mjs A`. |

`src/props.js`, `assets/props.json`, cameras and all existing scripts are unchanged. Shared terrain still supplies the loader's analytical ground height. Landscape/debris geometry lives outside `propRoot`; all eight A slots remain empty.

## Verification

- `npm run build` passes. Vite reports a nonblocking bundle-size advisory for the three.js bundle.
- `node scripts/shoot.mjs A` passes for all three cameras with no browser or shader errors.
- `node scripts/verify.mjs` passes: intercepts B/C asset requests with an in-memory offset test mesh, verifies all eight heights, horizontal centers and ground contacts for both groups; also verifies empty A slots, advancing wave time, and mouse-driven OrbitControls. The fixture is never saved into the asset directories.
- Real B/C GLBs were not supplied. Loader failures retain their empty markers and report warnings/results; the screenshot script treats browser resource errors as failure after saving the views, so missing assets cannot silently qualify as a successful group capture.

## Known weaknesses

- Water is an efficient analytical approximation, not a fluid simulation. The visible sandy bottom and caustics are evaluated inside the Water shader rather than through a refractive scene-depth buffer; submerged props will not refract correctly.
- Foam animates along a fixed shoreline; it does not physically advance over the sand. Swells are small, with planar reflection approximations.
- Landforms and canopy are procedural approximations; individual foliage clusters remain discernible. Sand and caustic patterns can reveal repetition at close range. Wet sand uses an analytical sky-colored Fresnel approximation, not a second planar reflection pass.
- Bounding-box grounding uses the slot center's ground height. Very wide future props may need per-asset adjustments to avoid local dune intersections. Animated/compressed GLB extensions have not been tested.
- SwiftShader captures prioritize reproducibility, not real-device frame-rate measurement.

## Group A

All eight slots now contain code-generated three.js models. `src/props.js` dispatches the A builders in `src/props-a.js`, batches geometry by material, and normalizes each model to the exact configured height, horizontal slot center, and analytical ground height. Slot markers retain the exact `pos` values from `assets/props.json`. Seeded geometry, canvas grain/chipped-paint maps, and a procedural basalt shader are the only asset sources: no model files, image assets, remote requests, or CDNs are used by A. B/C loading behavior is unchanged.

The shared `src/main.js`, water, sky, sand, lighting, post-processing, cameras, and slot configuration are unchanged.

| Prop | Approach | Triangles |
| --- | --- | ---: |
| `palm_tall` | Curved, tapered tube trunk with growth rings and crown sheaths; 15 arched fronds made from separate tapered leaflets; seven coconuts. | 17,088 |
| `palm_pair` | Two individually seeded palms with different heights and opposing leans from a shared base. | 30,288 |
| `rocks` | Seven irregular, smoothed basalt meshes, separately grounded; vertex color variation and shader pores; ray-placed open barnacle shells with dark apertures. | 25,340 |
| `boat` | Hollow tapered hull with seven blue strakes per side, separate inner wood surfaces, ribs, floorboards, three thwarts, gunwales, nails, oarlocks, and two stowed wooden oars. | 15,600 |
| `hut` | Short stilts, braces, individual floor/wall planks, doorway, side windows, steps, and seven overlapping courses of irregular palm thatch. | 9,896 |
| `umbrella` | Timber pole and radial ribs under layered straw thatch; two slatted loungers with raised backs, armrests, legs, support struts, and bolts. | 9,788 |
| `driftwood` | Curved irregular bleached trunk, longitudinal grooves, tapered broken branches/root forks, end faces, and splinters. | 7,192 |
| `lifeguard` | Splayed white supports and cross braces, elevated plank deck, railings, ladder, lookout seat, red plank roof, rescue cross, and lifebuoy. | 1,868 |

Total: **117,060 triangles**, counted from the final mesh geometry, excluding the shared scene and inspection floor. Counts are also saved in `shots/A/props/triangles.json`.

### Isolated inspection

With the development server running, open `http://localhost:5191/props.html?solo=boat` (substitute any slot id). This independent viewer uses a neutral grey background/floor, fixed studio lights, and a fixed three-quarter camera. Each model is uniformly scaled so its longest bounding-box dimension is three units; all use the same camera, ground baseline, 38-degree field of view, and 800×800 capture. This exposes the natural aspect-ratio differences rather than stretching narrow props. These studio settings do not affect the beach comparison.

```sh
node scripts/shoot.mjs A
node scripts/shoot-props.mjs
node scripts/props-contact.mjs r4
node scripts/verify.mjs
npm run build
```

Scene captures: `shots/A/{wide,beach,closeup}.png`. Individual renders: `shots/A/props/<slot>.png`. The contact-sheet utility uses local Python/Pillow solely to arrange verification screenshots; its output is never loaded as a scene asset.

### Three correction rounds

| Checkpoint | Review and corrections |
| --- | --- |
| `shots/A/r1.png` | Initial complete set. Lounger backs tilted downward; rocks were excessively faceted; driftwood ends were open; thatch looked like regular wooden pickets. |
| `shots/A/r2.png` | Round 1: corrected lounger back rotation, smoothed/refined rock topology, closed driftwood ends with splinters, widened palm leaflets, lowered protruding hut posts, and replaced broad regular thatch with finer, denser, varied strips. |
| `shots/A/r3.png` | Round 2: tapered and curved the driftwood with forked branches, added basalt pore shading, cut hut windows, added individual tower roof boards and thatch course relief. Batched meshes by material to reduce draw calls. |
| `shots/A/r4.png` | Round 3 plus final grounding review: irregular drooping thatch edges, open barnacle apertures and denser colonies, gentler driftwood branch taper, boat nails/oarlocks, lounger bolts, and a corrected transform reset after batching. Grounded each rock separately before assembling the cluster. Final scene and individual captures were regenerated. |

### Verification and remaining weaknesses

- `node scripts/shoot.mjs A` and `node scripts/shoot-props.mjs` complete without browser or shader errors.
- `node scripts/verify.mjs` now checks populated A slots as well as the B/C fixture loaders: all eight heights, horizontal centers, and ground contacts match within `1e-5`. Live water animation and OrbitControls remain operational.
- `npm run build` passes; Vite retains its nonblocking large-bundle advisory.
- Palm foliage and straw remain thin ribbon approximations, with no wind animation or subsurface scattering. Thatch still has an underlying conical silhouette, and palm crowns can look sparse at distance.
- Wood grain is procedural and repeated; it is not anatomically correct end grain on every face. The boat's strakes are thin surfaces and its underside is simplified. Driftwood forks are still visibly constructed at close inspection.
- Rock pores are shader detail rather than fully modeled cavities; barnacles repeat a small shell profile.
- The unchanged shared shadow map produces fine self-shadow patterns on small lounge slats and foliage. Large props are grounded at the slot's central terrain height, so individual feet can intersect uneven sand. The isolated viewer removes terrain variation but does not conceal those scene limitations.

## Explore mode

Open **http://localhost:5191/?explore=1&group=A** and press **點擊開始**. Explore is explicitly opt-in: a URL without `explore=1` retains OrbitControls; any `cam` parameter takes precedence and retains the original comparison view. The explore module and CSS load only in explore mode. Shared water, sky, terrain, lights, prop generators, fitting rules, and existing screenshot scripts are unchanged.

- WASD / arrows move relative to the camera; mouse looks around; Shift runs; Space jumps. V toggles third/first person. Esc releases pointer lock and pauses; click the start button to resume. While paused, the group buttons remain accessible.
- 1 / 2 / 3 or the segmented buttons switch A｜codex 程序化, B｜Tripo, C｜免費素材庫 in place. The HUD counts actual mesh triangles, excluding the landscape and avatar. Missing files leave empty slots and a visible missing count. Near loaded props, a label identifies the slot and source.
- M or the sound button mutes procedural wave/wind audio, created only after the initial click. P freezes the player and camera and hides the HUD; P again returns. Touch users can tap the lower-right corner to leave photo mode (the exit control is invisible until hovered/focused so captures remain clean).
- Touch devices have a left joystick, right drag-to-look region, jump button, view toggle, group buttons, and photo control.
- Ground contact uses `groundHeight()`. Water deeper than 0.65 m is blocked, shallow wading slows movement and emits pooled splash rings, and the cove is bounded at X −34…35 and Z ≤27. Expanded world-space slot boxes stop the player and shorten the third-person camera boom. Camera height is clamped above sand. A newly switched model that surrounds the player permits movement toward an exit without teleporting the player.

Implementation: `src/explore.js` and `src/explore.css`, with a small opt-in hook in `src/main.js`. Character geometry is shared, ten splash meshes are pooled, camera vectors are reused, collision boxes are built only after loading, and POI text changes only when its target/group changes. Group loads are serialized and up to three groups are cached to prevent repeated GPU allocation on revisits. The existing loader and its fitting rule remain untouched.

### Screenshot / feel iterations

1. `shots/explore/round1/`: initial screenshots showed an oversized character, high camera pitch, and floating-looking feet. Pulled the follow camera farther back, lowered its angle, added shoes and head shadows, and added a small walking bob. Kept paused HUD controls reachable after pointer unlock.
2. `shots/explore/round2/`: reviewed the improved walk views. Smoothed limb return when stopping, shortened source labels, and fixed the group-switch overlap case so a player can exit newly overlapping bounds. Final captures are `shots/explore/{start,walk1,walk2,group_switch}.png`; `mobile.png` checks the portrait touch layout.

## 看過現況後的方向

已看過 current/ 的 shells、ball、lounger、tower、boat、opensea、tidepool、headland 共 8 張截圖。現有旅程已有散步、撿拾、休息、登高、划船與觀察；較值得補的是「手碰到環境，留下一點短暫改變」。主沙灘適合近距離小互動，岬角林緣適合安靜停留，小島適合安排一個到達後的小回饋。

以下都採自由體驗，不強制加進原本 7 個任務，避免把 8–12 分鐘的放鬆時光變成更長的待辦清單。E 或手機互動鍵即可開始／離開，沒有失敗、分數與倒數。

## 排序與估工前提

依主觀「好玩程度 ÷ 工作量」排序；好玩以 1–5 分評估觸覺回饋、新鮮感與重玩意願，工作量權重為小＝1、中＝2、大＝4，僅用來比較優先順序。同分時優先選擇能補足現有體驗的內容。小約 1–2 個工作天、中約 3–5 天、大約 1–2 週，是沿用現有系統下的粗估，包含基本 A／B／C 素材整理與桌機／手機檢查；素材搜尋、生成重試與精修可能增加時間。

| 排名 | 點子 | 好玩 | 工作量 | 比值 | 建議 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 濕沙留一筆 | 4 | 小 | 4.0 | **最推薦；idea1.png** |
| 2 | 輕碰竹風鈴 | 3 | 小 | 3.0 | **最推薦；idea2.png** |
| 3 | 堆一座會回到海裡的沙堡 | 5 | 中 | 2.5 | **最推薦；idea3.png** |
| 4 | 把風箏交給海風 | 5 | 中 | 2.5 | **最推薦；idea4.png** |
| 5 | 把空貝殼排成小花 | 4 | 中 | 2.0 | 第二批 |
| 6 | 岬角望遠鏡 | 2 | 小 | 2.0 | 有餘裕再加 |
| 7 | 小島上的海螺聽筒 | 2 | 小 | 2.0 | 輕量到達回饋 |
| 8 | 打一串水漂 | 4 | 中 | 2.0 | 第二批 |
| 9 | 林緣吊床 | 3 | 中 | 1.5 | 與躺椅重疊，後做 |
| 10 | 淺水玻璃觀察筒 | 3 | 大 | 0.75 | 先保留 |

### 1. 濕沙留一筆｜最推薦

- **玩家怎麼玩：** 在固定濕沙區按 E，角色蹲下，用木枝畫一道螺旋；再次互動可換成波紋或圓圈。畫完能站著看海浪慢慢抹平，也能直接離開。
- **新物件／動作：** 一根短木枝；沿固定曲線移動手腕的蹲姿片段。沙紋是地表效果，不是新模型。
- **可重用：** 撿貝殼的蹲下姿勢、手部 IK、腳印的地表印記概念、岸浪位置與道具探測。腳印若只支援獨立印章，仍需補筆畫顯示。
- **加分原因：** 把既有海浪變成互動的收尾；短短幾秒就有「我曾在這裡」的感覺。
- **工作量：小。** 首版只有固定位置與三款預設筆畫，不做滑鼠自由繪圖、文字輸入或地形雕刻；抹除依既有浪線遮罩淡出。

### 2. 輕碰竹風鈴｜最推薦

- **玩家怎麼玩：** 草傘下掛一串風鈴，按 E 輕碰下方木片，聽竹管依序敲響。也可坐回旁邊躺椅，讓聲音陪著海浪。
- **新物件／動作：** 一組完整竹風鈴模型；短暫抬手觸碰。竹管可分成同一模型內的子物件。
- **可重用：** 草傘懸掛點、道具探測、手部 IK、既有聲音開關與距離音量（若未提供距離音量，補簡單衰減即可）。
- **加分原因：** 第一次讓海灘道具對玩家的手發出回應；也讓既有休息點更有辨識度。
- **工作量：小。** 固定音序與衰減擺動；不做碰撞發聲。三組模型即使沒有可分離竹管，也能先用整體小幅擺動完成首版。

### 3. 堆一座會回到海裡的沙堡｜最推薦

- **玩家怎麼玩：** 在岸邊小沙堆旁按 E，角色蹲下拍實沙子，分三次露出低矮沙堡的輪廓。完成後可以欣賞，也能主動選擇讓下一波浪把它帶回海裡。
- **新物件／動作：** 一座約膝高、單塔加矮牆的沙堡；雙手拍沙短動作。不加水桶、鏟子或旗子，維持單一模型主角。
- **可重用：** 蹲姿、手部 IK、揚沙效果、互動階段、岸浪接觸位置。
- **加分原因：** 有清楚的創作成果，也有溫柔的告別；比單純撿取多了一點期待。
- **工作量：中。** 同一模型從沙面下分階段升起並以沙塵遮掩；被浪帶走時下沉、淡出，不做粒子堆積或真實侵蝕。圖中是完成後最後一次拍實的瞬間。

### 4. 把風箏交給海風｜最推薦

- **玩家怎麼玩：** 在開闊沙地按 E 拿起風箏線，角色固定站位，風箏自行慢慢升空；再按 E 平穩收回。玩家只需轉動鏡頭，看風箏與影子滑過海灘。
- **新物件／動作：** 一只珊瑚橘與米白色菱形風箏，尾帶包含在同一模型；雙手握線姿勢。線由共用曲線呈現，不另做線軸模型。
- **可重用：** 道具探測、手部 IK、固定互動站位、相機旋轉與既有陰影。
- **加分原因：** 把視線從沙灘拉到天空；風箏、長線與影子形成容易記住的畫面。
- **工作量：中。** 預設升空、盤旋與收回曲線，尾帶只做簡單時間變形；沒有風力求解、放線技巧或墜落失敗。活動區避開椰樹與救生塔，首版不開放拿著跑。

### 5. 把空貝殼排成小花

- **玩家怎麼玩：** 撿完貝殼後，在漂流木旁按 E，將空貝殼逐枚擺成一朵小花。再按一次可換成圓環，隨時能離開。
- **新物件／動作：** 無必要新模型，重用空貝殼；蹲下放置的手勢與固定擺放位置。
- **可重用：** 貝殼收集狀態、撿拾姿勢、手部 IK、道具探測。
- **加分原因：** 讓已收集的東西有可見去處；只用空貝殼，不搬動潮池生物。
- **工作量：中。** 兩組預設排列，貝殼以同一時間軸逐枚出現；需補收集與展示狀態銜接，不做自由佈置或背包系統。

### 6. 岬角望遠鏡

- **玩家怎麼玩：** 走到林緣的固定觀景點，按 E 扶住立柱望遠鏡，看遠方小島與船邊的浮標；退出就回到原本第三人稱。
- **新物件／動作：** 一座鏡筒與立柱整合的望遠鏡；站姿前傾、雙手扶鏡。
- **可重用：** 救生塔看海的觀看邏輯、相機視角、手部 IK、現有景物。
- **加分原因：** 給岬角一個停留理由，也讓小島距離更有感。
- **工作量：小。** 首版固定望向既有地標，只縮小相機視野，不做新觀察圖鑑、遠端生物觸發或鏡片二次渲染。

### 7. 小島上的海螺聽筒

- **玩家怎麼玩：** 登島後，在岸邊漂流木上發現一枚空海螺；按 E 拿到耳邊，聽一小段低沉共鳴，再放回原位。
- **新物件／動作：** 一枚空海螺模型；拿起、靠近耳邊、放回三段短姿勢。
- **可重用：** 撿拾與物件附著、手部 IK、聲音播放、島上互動探測。
- **加分原因：** 為划船到達提供安靜而私人的回饋；共鳴是氣氛音效，不暗示殼裡真的裝著海浪。
- **工作量：小。** 固定音效與姿勢，不加入收藏或帶走功能。

### 8. 打一串水漂

- **玩家怎麼玩：** 岸邊按 E 撿一顆扁石，自動側身拋出，看石頭連跳三下後沉入海裡。每次都成功，不比距離與次數。
- **新物件／動作：** 一顆扁石；一段側拋動作。
- **可重用：** 蹲下拾取、手部 IK、涉水漣漪與水花、道具探測。
- **加分原因：** 連續三次水面回饋很直覺，能把已經漂亮的水面變成可玩的細節。
- **工作量：中。** 石頭沿固定拋物線段前進，各落點查詢解析式浪高；不靠剛體反彈。新投擲姿勢與水花節奏需要調整，因此排在後面。

### 9. 林緣吊床

- **玩家怎麼玩：** 在岬角林緣坐進一張自帶木架的吊床，緩緩躺下、輕輕晃動；按 E 隨時起身。
- **新物件／動作：** 一組獨立木架吊床；坐下轉躺與起身的過渡姿勢。
- **可重用：** 躺椅休息狀態、身體定位、IK 與相機。
- **加分原因：** 可以從葉影下看海，拓展岬角的停留感；但體驗和躺椅較接近。
- **工作量：中。** 支架不動，床布與角色共同做小幅預設擺動；同一資產需可辨識床體與支架，不做布料物理。

### 10. 淺水玻璃觀察筒

- **玩家怎麼玩：** 在固定及膝淺水點俯身握住觀察筒，透過玻璃底看清沙紋與小魚，放開便回到波光閃動的水面。
- **新物件／動作：** 一個帶雙把手的玻璃底觀察筒；俯身握持姿勢。小魚可由既有素材縮小重用，但需另排固定游動路徑。
- **可重用：** 淺水場景、水面著色、手部 IK、觀察切換。
- **加分原因：** 讓玩家感受到「遮掉反光後，水下變清楚」的探索驚喜。
- **工作量：大。** 需要局部水面遮罩或額外渲染視角，還要檢查透明排序與手機效能；首輪不建議做。

## 不加任務，也能更有生命感的 5 個點綴

1. **岸邊沙蟹探頭：** 一個小沙蟹模型重複使用，在固定洞口依時間探頭、退回；角色接近時記錄觸發時間，播放固定退洞片段，不做尋路或追逐。
2. **遠處海鳥掠過：** 同一隻鳥複製少量個體，沿固定曲線滑翔；翅膀用簡單週期動作，偶爾有遠近變化的叫聲，不讓鳥成為新的收集目標。
3. **海風帶動葉影：** 椰葉小幅週期擺動，將微弱風聲與葉影變化對齊同一時間值；維持午後光照，不額外開發完整日夜循環。
4. **浪退後的濕沙亮帶：** 讓浪剛退去的位置短暫加深顏色、降低粗糙度，再逐漸恢復，直接強化現有岸浪與腳印的觸感，不新增模型。
5. **依位置分層的環境聲：** 岸邊浪聲、林緣葉聲、船身輕響分開淡入淡出；從固定素材與固定相位播放，保留聲音關閉功能，避免突然的大音量。

## A／B／C 比較與可重播原則

- 每個新物件先訂一致外框尺寸、原點、朝向與互動接觸點；A 程序模型、B 生成模型、C 免費素材都對齊同一規格。C 若缺完全相同素材，以相同功能與輪廓的簡單物件替代，並記錄差異；素材授權另外確認。
- 木枝、竹風鈴、沙堡、風箏各是一個可獨立交付的模型資產；一個資產可含子物件，不代表完全不可分件。接觸點可在匯入後共用設定，避免要求生成模型自帶骨架。
- 沙紋、風箏線、水花、音效與互動邏輯由三組共用；差異集中在素材，不替某一組額外加漂亮特效。
- 所有動態依共用時間 t 評估。玩家互動只記錄觸發時間 t₀、選擇與階段，片段進度取 t−t₀；逐格錄影使用相同初始狀態及輸入紀錄。不要使用牆鐘時間、每幀累積亂數或物理引擎結果。

## Water v2

Water and sand shading now live together in `src/water.js`, wired into `src/main.js`. The existing sun/sky, exposure, lights, camera presets, terrain functions/mesh, props/fitting, slots and Explore/compare/hub behavior are unchanged. The only time source is `water.material.uniforms.time`; the sand material references **that exact uniform object**. `?time=` and `window.__TIME__` therefore freeze/seek waves, normals, foam, caustics, swash and drying together. No simulation history, random animation state, texture downloads or wall-clock-driven shader inputs are used.

### Techniques

- Four directional Gerstner components (19, 11.3, 6.7 and 3.8 m wavelengths; offshore amplitudes 0.29, 0.16, 0.085 and 0.045 m) give actual horizontal/vertical displacement and analytical wave normals. Lagoon attenuation and a separate asymmetric shoaling bore produce readable nearshore crests. Troughs are bounded above the existing seabed to prevent disconnected water strips. Distant displacement/detail fades before coarse mesh rows can alias.
- A single coast-following water grid concentrates 35 cm rows in the surf and coarsens offshore. It contains **110,767 vertices / 220,160 triangles**, versus 204,800 triangles previously (+7.5%). The terrain itself is untouched.
- Domain-warped, world-space procedural gradient noise replaces the tiled normal texture. Four scales, with different rotations and advection directions, move independently; fine detail diminishes with viewing distance. There is no repeating normal-map tile.
- Breaking foam follows the same crest phase as the shoaling wave, with irregular caps, cellular-looking lace, small bubbles and a dispersing wake. A fast uprush and slower backwash move a conforming thin water sheet approximately 0–2.7 m onto the beach. Its ragged edge and foam coverage vary spatially. The cycle is about 4.62 s, with alongshore phase offsets.
- Sand keeps its warm hue while wetness lowers albedo/roughness. A stateless inverse-smoothstep calculation of time since retreat leaves a mottled damp mark that gradually dries. Fresnel sheen is strongest in the fresh film; the old uniform gray strip is gone.
- RGB Beer–Lambert absorption, an angle-dependent optical path, refracted procedural bottom coordinates, restrained moving caustics, shallow crest tint, Schlick Fresnel reflection and sun-aligned glitter replace the previous fixed color/reflection blend. Reflections use a bounded projected reflected ray and filtered planar samples; their sky fallback matches the existing sky gradient. The original 512×512 planar reflection pass is retained.

Wave construction was informed by [NVIDIA GPU Gems: Effective Water Simulation from Physical Models](https://developer.nvidia.com/gpugems/gpugems/part-i-natural-effects/chapter-1-effective-water-simulation-physical-models). The nearshore visual reference was [Mohamed Sameeh's Maldives surf photograph](https://unsplash.com/photos/waves-of-water-at-beach-8iKpG2BmjOA). Neither reference supplies runtime assets.

### Remaining limitations

This is an analytical lagoon approximation, not a fluid solver: breakers do not overturn into tubes or throw particle spray, and foam does not collide with individual props. Bottom refraction/caustics are procedural, so submerged models are not refracted through a scene-depth buffer. Reflections remain planar with a bounded ray approximation; steep nearshore waves and grazing views can reveal stretching, and the existing stylized clouds/landforms remain visible in reflections. Wet-sand drying is a deterministic cyclic approximation, not an accumulated physical moisture simulation. The unchanged sand tessellation can reveal minor water-film contact errors at distant/coarse shoreline sections. Real RTX profiling remains outstanding.

## Game mode

Open **http://localhost:5191/game.html** (also linked as **遊戲模式** on the hub). Defaults to **B / Tripo**; `?group=A` or `?group=C` selects another source. Press **開始玩**, finish the five tasks in any order, and return from the boat to see the completion time and **再玩一次**. A normal walk around the beach plus the approximately one-minute boat round trip is designed for a 3–5 minute visit. The automated run teleports between shore activities, so its ~1:21 simulated time is not a human playtime measurement.

### Controls and tasks
